text:
Alex W: FYI support ticket #5482 — Acme reporting p99 jumps (~2x) starting ~09:15 UTC after last config push. They say short prompts see long tails. https://acme.example/trace :worried:
Morgan (eng-platform): can you paste the exact config? continuous batching/grace/linger values?
Alex W: pushing logs... small snippet: `p95: 120ms, p99: 980ms` on model-x-prod-1 before fix. After rollback of hold-window to 10ms p99 dropped to ~210ms.
Priya (support): customer repro steps: send 50 req/s of 1-2 token completions for 10s, wait 30s, repeat. We reproduced in staging and see same tail.
Dana S: sounds like grace/linger + tiny prompts -> oversized KV-cache batching and then long wait. Try reducing grace and batch_hold to avoid greedy coalescing. Example quick patch I tried in staging:```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  grace_ms: 8
  max_hold_ms: 10
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
```
Morgan (eng-platform): thanks. can you share the trace for the big p99 samples? want to confirm whether it's waiting for batch fill vs kernel overhead.
Alex W: attached trace shows "wait_for_coalesce" spans dominating: 650-900ms on p99 entries. Also auth and billing were green.
Priya (support): customer on dedicated plan — they hit production during our push window, escalated to SE. We applied Dana's quick patch at 09:32 and customer reported perf improved by 09:35.
Morgan (eng-platform): good. let's add a short-lived canary rollout for the patch on 10% of traffic and collect p95/p99 over 30m. If stable, roll to 100% and add a config guardrail to prevent grace_ms > 50ms for small-prompt models.
Dana S: agree. also add a telemetry tag to distinguish "tiny_prompt" requests so optimizer can suggest quantization/caching.
Alex W: quick mitigation note I put in runbook: "If p99 spike with short prompts, reduce grace_ms -> 8-12ms and max_hold_ms -> 10ms; monitor coalesce_wait spans."
latency-bot: alert: p99 for model-x-prod-1 dropped from 980ms -> 220ms after patch (09:35). :white_check_mark:
Morgan (eng-platform): follow-ups: 1) canary + guardrail, 2) add customer-facing postmortem blurb, 3) long-term: evaluate adaptive grace that scales with observed token lengths. I'll file a ticket and tag eng-sre/ops.
Priya (support): customer satisfied but wants root cause writeup + timeline. I'll draft & loop SE. :thumbsup:
Alex W: thanks everyone. saving logs and repro steps to the ticket.
Dana S: will add the config snippet to ops-templates and create an automated check in the deploy pipeline to warn on dangerous grace/batch combos.
Morgan (eng-platform): closing triage thread in 30m unless new regressions.
